Homemade Marzipan

Served at: Sinterklaas Arrival (Intocht)

Makes about 1.5 pounds (680g)Prep 20 min

Marzipan is a beloved sweet treat during the Sinterklaas festivities in the Netherlands, often shaped into whimsical figures like pigs, letters, or fruits. Its arrival, much like Sinterklaas himself, signals the start of a joyous season, making it a perfect confection to enjoy as you welcome the good saint during the Intocht.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (200g) blanched almond flour
  • 2 cups (240g) confectioners' (powdered) sugar, plus more for dusting
  • 1 large egg white (about 30g)
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5ml) almond extract
  • 1/4 teaspoon (1.25ml) rose water (optional)

Method

  1. In a large bowl, whisk together the almond flour and confectioners' sugar until well combined and no lumps remain.
  2. In a separate small bowl, lightly whisk the egg white with the almond extract and rose water (if using).
  3. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Mix with a spatula or your hands until a crumbly dough forms.
  4. Turn the dough out onto a clean, lightly powdered sugar-dusted surface.
  5. Knead the marzipan for about 5-7 minutes, or until it is smooth, pliable, and no longer sticky. If it's too sticky, add a little more powdered sugar; if too dry, add a tiny bit more egg white or water, a few drops at a time.
  6. Once smooth, wrap the marzipan tightly in plastic wrap to prevent it from drying out.
  7. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before shaping. This makes it easier to work with.
  8. When ready to use, let it come to room temperature for a few minutes, then shape into desired Sinterklaas figures, letters, or treats.

Tips

  • For colored marzipan, knead in a few drops of gel food coloring after the initial mixing phase.
  • Store homemade marzipan wrapped tightly in plastic wrap in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks, or freeze for up to 3 months.
  • Dip shaped marzipan figures in melted dark chocolate for an extra festive and delicious touch.
